name: kusto-mcp

tools.name: initialize-connection
tools.description: Creates connection to an ADX cluster

cluster_url.description: The URL of the Kusto cluster

tools.name: show-tables
tools.description: List tables in the current database

tableName.description: The name of the table to get the schema for

tools.name: execute-query
tools.description: Runs KQL queries and returns results. If you have not inspected the table yet, call show-table first to see its columns. By default, limits results to 20 rows to prevent context overflow. Use the "limit" parameter to specify a different maximum. If results are marked as partial, consider revising your query to use aggregations, filters, or summarizations. Optionally set "purpose" to the closest intent.

purpose.description: Optional analytics hint: why you are running this query, e.g. schema_discovery, point_lookup, exploration, incident_investigation, service_health, reporting_pipeline, bulk_extract, other. Omit if unsure. Never put query text or names here.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return (default: 20)

tools.name: show-functions
tools.description: List functions in the current database

tools.name: show-function
tools.description: Show details of a specific function, including its code and parameters

functionName.description: The name of the function to get details for

tools.name: report-issue
tools.description: Report a bug or request a feature for kusto-mcp on GitHub. Returns a pre-filled GitHub issue link you open in your browser and submit under your own GitHub account — no GitHub token is used or stored, and no Kusto connection is required.

title.description: Short summary line for the GitHub issue

body.description: Full description (Markdown): what happened, expected vs actual behavior, and steps to reproduce.

includeDiagnostics.description: Append non-sensitive environment info (kusto-mcp/node/OS/MCP-client versions, connection state, response format, write mode). Never includes cluster URL, database, identity, query text, or results.

kusto-mcp reports anonymous usage telemetry (tool usage, latency, error types, version/OS, a random install id, and salted one-way hashes of your Azure tenant/user id for distinct counts) to the maintainer. No query text, results, or raw identity are collected, except an optional `purpose` hint, which is sent as written. See README > Telemetry.
